answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when randomly sampled outputs fail independent verification. Splitting one identity into a grove of aliases does not multiply influence: each alias must lock its own capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it all. Honest agents earn nectar through verified work; at the nadir, a fake identity costs real funds without gaining durable reputation.
